note: Triennial election of Irvinestown Rural District Council, polled Thursday 5 June 1958. No contests. The Impartial Reporter of 22 May 1958, p. 7, states that 'all the members of Irvinestown Rural Council have again been nominated without change'. The members are recorded where a selection list or a report of the new council's meetings names them, each division inferred from the 1955 return (Fermanagh Herald, 4 June 1955, p. 8). Filled from the Impartial Reporter's reports of Unionist selections (1, 8 and 15 May 1958): Ballinamallard, Drumrush, Kesh, Clonelly, Brookhill, Magheraculmoney and Lack; each was returned unopposed (Impartial Reporter, 22 May 1958, p. 7). Recorded for Nationalist-held divisions from the selection lists and first-meeting reports in the Fermanagh Herald: Castlecaldwell, Garrison and Irvinestown. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Churchill, Killadeas, Aghamuldowney and Inishmacsaint. division inferred from the 2 June 1955 return (Edward C. Corrigan); the Impartial Reporter, 19 June 1958, p. 7 names the member as returned, sitting on the new council. Printed 'E. C. Corrigan'. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Churchill' to Church Hill (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Church Hill; the rounds were filed as Churchhill (1924, 1927, 1930, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1961, 1964); Churchill (1933, 1949, 1952, 1955, 1958). This round was filed as 'Churchill', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (churchill) answers with a redirect to this one.
